name: Cacao Type
description: Custom confectionery pitch with sculptural chocolate letters and folded order sheets.

slides.title:
The gift should
say something.
items: A name. A date. A small thank-you.
Event planners repeatedly coordinate artwork, packaging and delivery across separate suppliers. A late wording change can trigger three new approvals.
Cacao Type puts the chocolate message, box and dispatch date into one approved order.

slides.title: A box with a point of view
items: Choose the letter set, filling and sleeve. Approve a proof with the exact contents before production starts.
One order number follows the batch through packing and dispatch.

slides.title: Built in the mold
items: A stable alphabet gives planners custom wording without a new tool for every event.
Approved recipes and a retained batch record keep repeat orders consistent.

slides.title: The order has four decisions
items: Names, initials or a short phrase. The proof locks spelling and piece count.
Choose from the current production menu. Ingredient information travels with the proof.
Match the event artwork and confirm the delivery contact on the same sheet.
Reserve the batch slot after approval. Dispatch follows the agreed delivery window.

slides.title: The batch gets more efficient
items: Illustrative production minutes per six-piece box
Larger approved batches spread mold preparation and packing setup across more boxes. Track labor separately from ingredients.

slides.title:
Meet planners where
the brief begins
items: Offer a paid tasting kit to boutique event agencies. The kit includes the available alphabet, filling menu and a proof example.
Twelve agencies placing six £2,400 orders a year would produce £172,800 in annual sales.

slides.title: The production calendar is the promise
items: Spelling, allergens, quantity and address are confirmed together.
The production lead checks the recipe record and retained sample.
Packing counts and the courier handover are logged to the order.

slides.title: Two signatures on every batch
items: Owns the menu, batch release and packing standards. Trains the first two production hires.
Owns proofs, agency accounts and delivery promises. Keeps changes tied to the approved order.

slides.title: Earn the repeat order
items: Complete thirty paid orders. Record actual labor minutes, breakage and delivery performance for every batch.
Target twelve active agencies, a 40% reorder rate and fewer than 2% damaged boxes at handover.
Expansion follows repeat demand and measured kitchen capacity.

slides.title:
A sweeter way
to leave a mark.
items:
£150k kitchen and molds
£120k production team
£80k tasting kits and working capital
Twelve months to twelve active agency partners. Fictional business and financial model. AI-generated artwork.
